key_insight: A tree-anchored weighted combination reduced photovoltaic forecast MAE by 3.21% versus LightGBM alone across 15–240-minute horizons.
engineering_relevance: Selective combination can improve short-term solar power forecasts without requiring every candidate model to contribute.
method: Combine LightGBM with seven neural predictors using nonnegative weights that sum to one.
Fit shared cross-horizon weights to MAE, allowing unhelpful candidates to receive zero weight.
Test horizon-specific weights, alternative losses and a bounded neural correction.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used 56,078 windows from two co-located public PVDAQ systems; the historical shared-MAE combination improved on the tree, while the latest neural correction added no further MAE reduction.
watch_item: Both analyses reused a previously inspected evaluation period, so independent validation is needed before assuming broader gains.
paper_title: Reducing Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Forecast Error through Tree-Anchored Expert Combination
